summary: Neso (Ancient Greek: Νησώ) is one of the fifty Nereids, marine-nymph daughters of Nereus and the Oceanid Doris. Hesiod names her late in the Nereid catalogue of the Theogony; Apollodorus repeats her among the sea-sisters. The name suggests an island-nymph, but she has no independent myth beyond the catalogue.
etymology: Neso (Νησώ) is glossed "the island-goddess" or, in some modern handbooks, "nimble," from the root associated with νῆσος (nēsos), "island."

sections.heading: Among the Nereids
paragraphs: Hesiod's Theogony lists Neso among the daughters of Nereus and Doris — after Psamathe of charming figure and divine Menippe, before Eupompe, Themisto, Pronoe, and Nemertes who has the mind of her deathless father. Apollodorus' Bibliotheca preserves her in the same fifty-sister roll.

Like many catalogue Nereids she is a name without a separate adventure: her identity is genealogical and etymological, marking the sea's island realm beside better-attested sisters such as Thetis, Amphitrite, and Galatea.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (neso) is the Nereid. Other figures named Neso include the mother of the Cumaean Sibyl in later notices and a daughter of King Teucer — distinct mortals or local eponyms, not the Hesiodic sea-nymph.
